centre.label: Centre Click · OP1
centre.note: The printed parts use the R23 meshes. The OP1 board, plug and switch use estimated dimensions.

steps.title: Slide In the Stock Board
steps.caption: Plug the switch and white cable into the OP1 board. Slide the board in from the front with the paddle lifted away.

steps.title: Fit the Paddle
steps.caption: Lower the paddle between the two hinge sides and line up the holes.

steps.title: Slide In the Hinge Pin
steps.caption: Use a short piece of 1.75 mm filament through both sides of the hinge.

steps.title: Press and Release
steps.caption: The small ridge presses the switch. The side stops take the load at the end of the press.

steps.title: Connect the Click
steps.caption: Find COM and NO with a meter on the unplugged harness. Connect COM to GND and NO to D8 on the XIAO.

key.label: Four Choc Keys · R23
key.note: Fit the four Choc switches here. Choose Centre Click to fit the OP1 board and paddle.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Solder the Sockets Off the Holder
steps.caption: With the holder off the rod and upside down on the bench, solder each socket's two wires outside the holder. Keep solder on the terminal tabs, not above them.

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Left Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the left edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

checks.moving: socket_0 with the stated terminal solder allowance

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Right Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the right edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

checks.moving: socket_2 with the stated terminal solder allowance

steps.title: Push Up the Upper Sockets
steps.caption: Bring each socket up about 1 mm away from the rod position, so its inner solder joint passes beside the ring arm. 2 mm below the seat, move it in and press it up.

socket_3.moving: socket_3 with the stated terminal solder allowance

socket_4.moving: socket_4 with the stated terminal solder allowance

steps.title: Tape Every Socket
steps.caption: Lay one strip of polyimide tape across each socket and its wires onto the backplate, as on R16. Press the tape ends onto the backplate with a flat tool. Keep pressure off the guard runners. The tape insulates the solder from the rod and holds the socket.

steps.title: Press In the Switches
steps.caption: Back each socket from below with a finger or flat tool, then press each switch in from above until it clicks into the plate.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the wired holder onto the rod end-first. The rod runs through the two rings behind the lower row; the guard has no ring of its own.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Final position. The index finger rests on the rod between the inner runners; the runners sit under the lower sockets' outer terminals.

xiao.label: XIAO holder · R20 body + keeper
xiao.note: The board and its raised parts use Seeed's measured dimensions. Solder and fitted wires vary.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Lay In the Board
steps.caption: Tilt the near end of the board up about 6 degrees, slide the USB end under the two far fingers, then lower the near end onto its ledges. Side wires stay outside the walls. Underside solder must leave room: see the clearance map in geometry-checks.json.

steps.title: Find the Prongs and Ears
steps.caption: The two prongs lie over the bare board corners. The side ears slide in the holder grooves. The spring tab underneath catches the holder ridge.

steps.title: Slide On the Keeper
steps.caption: Check that the board sits flat on its ledges. If solder makes it rock or sit high, stop before fitting the keeper. With the ears in the side grooves, push the keeper over the near end. The tongue bends up over the ridge and clicks down behind it.

tongue.strain_note: Momentary, during the click only; zero when seated. Linear point-load estimate from CAD sizes, layers along the beam (keeper prints flat). Not a measured PETG strain limit, creep or fatigue result.

removal.documented: Pull by the ears (R18 README). The 45-degree ridge face lifts the tongue on the way out.
removal.tongue_lift_option: Geometrically sufficient (full-route overlap above). No lift tab exists; access through the 0.6 mm slit and force are unverified.

checks.note: Overlaps use the exported meshes with the drawn tongue bend; the bend is a visual beam model.

steps.title: Check the Catch
steps.caption: When fully seated, the tooth sits behind the ridge and the spring tab is flat again. Pull back gently to feel the catch. If it slides out freely after seating, check that the tooth and ridge are clear.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the holder onto the rod end-first. The USB-C port, antenna and reset button stay accessible.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Board held by the side walls, cheeks and near stops, and kept down by the keeper.

steps.title: Removing the Keeper
steps.caption: Pull back on both ears. The ridge is 45 degrees on this side too, so the tongue rides up and lets go. Take the keeper off before lifting the board.

xiao_latch.label: XIAO keeper latch · cutaway
xiao_latch.note: Side section of the R22 keeper and holder. The side grooves are outside this slice. The bend is an illustration from the CAD.

steps.title: Find the Tooth
steps.caption: The orange tooth hangs from the spring tab. The blue ridge is part of the holder.

steps.title: Push Until It Clicks
steps.caption: Push along the side grooves. The orange tab bends up as its tooth rides over the blue ridge.

tongue.strain_note: Momentary, during the click only; zero when seated. Linear point-load estimate from CAD sizes, layers along the beam (keeper prints flat). Not a measured PETG strain limit, creep or fatigue result.

removal.documented: Pull by the ears (R18 README). The 45-degree ridge face lifts the tongue on the way out.
removal.tongue_lift_option: Geometrically sufficient (full-route overlap above). No lift tab exists; access through the 0.6 mm slit and force are unverified.

checks.note: Overlaps use the exported meshes with the drawn tongue bend; the bend is a visual beam model.

steps.title: Check the Catch
steps.caption: The tooth drops behind the ridge. Check for a little resistance when you pull back gently.

steps.title: Pull Out by the Ears
steps.caption: Pull evenly on the two side ears. The tooth rides back over the ridge and the tab springs flat.

battery.label: Battery holder · R22
battery.note: The cell is drawn at the manufacturer maximum envelope.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Insert the Cell
steps.caption: Slide the cell in, leads last. Bring the leads through the centre opening.

steps.title: Drop In the Door
steps.caption: Push the door straight down into its two slots until the centre tooth clicks under the lip. R22 has a longer lead-in at the slot tops, so the tooth is pushed aside more gradually. If it is still too stiff, use the trial door, which has a shallower tooth.

checks.note: Overlap near the bottom is the catch tooth flexing over the lip (designed snap), not a clash.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the holder onto the rod end-first.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Cell held by the walls and teeth without pressure; door latched.
